newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian forces kill over 50 guerrillas - reports.
newsitem.headline: Algerian forces kill over 50 guerrillas - reports.

text.p: Algerian security forces have killed at least 53 Moslem guerrillas in two separate strikes on their strongholds in Algiers and the western province of Relizane, Algerian residents and a newspaper said on Sunday.

Government forces killed 43 Moslem guerrillas on Saturday at the end a three day search operation in Relizane province, some 300 km (180 miles) south of Algiers, said the Algerian evening newspaper Le Soir d'Algerie.

Those killed belonged to Algeria's ruthless guerrilla faction, the Armed Islamic Group (GIA), and until recently had been led by Kada Bencheiha, the group's western region local commander, said the newspaper.
Bencheiha was shot dead three months ago by the security forces, it added.
Le Soir d'Algerie said the security forces recovered 12 assault rifles, seven sawn-off shotguns, ammunition and homemade bombs.

In the Algerian capital, security forces backed by crack army troops killed at least 10 Moslem rebels in a 12-hour-siege in the Algiers Casbah, a rebel bastion in the old centre of the capital, residents said.
The security forces ringed the Casbah neighbourhood shortly after Moslem guerrillas shot dead three policemen in Algiers on Saturday and fled into the area's narrow streets.
"The siege started at about 11.30 a.m. (1030 GMT) on Saturday before being lifted at about midnight (2300 GMT)," said one resident.
The security forces closed off the area to stop civilians being caught in the crossfire, he said.
The authorities have made no comment on the violence.
Residents said security forces were out in force recently, hunting down guerrillas ahead of the June 5 parliamentary elections.
Last month, security forces fired rockets into one rebel hideout, killing eight people inside. The authorities suspected them of killing Algeria's top union leader Abdelhak Benhamouda on January 28.
President Liamine Zeroual has promised politicians the government will ensure security for the poll.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
